sampling_model.design: Two randomized regime studies report complete \(2\times2\) tables, one under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\) and one under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\).
sampling_model.units: The population version treats \(A\) and \(B\) as exact laws of one SCM; the optional sampling result uses multinomial frequency tables of sizes \(nA\) and \(nB\).
sampling_model.treatment: The first regime fixes \(Z=0\) and leaves \(X\) natural; the second fixes \(X=0\) and leaves \(Z\) natural.
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity of all eight population cells implies \(0<p,r<1\), \(0<a<p\), and \(0<b<r\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance functions are estimated. The optional interval uses only empirical multinomial cells and simultaneous concentration.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Minimization or maximization of the produced polynomial program gives sharp lower or upper bounds on the declared target.
Counterfactual consistency of overlapping categorical marginal SCMs restricts the admissible marginal and joint SCMs.
Every categorical SCM has a finite canonical SCM with the same graph and all the same counterfactual distributions.
EMCC returns fully specified compatible SCMs whose counterfactual range approximates the actual bounds from inside.
The global extrema of a response-function linear program occur at vertices of its feasible polytope.

body.tldr: For two complete experiments on the binary collider with two independent shared roots and private outcome noise, arbitrary normalized tables \(A,B\), including structural zeros, are compatible exactly when \(-(1-p)r\le a-b\le p(1-r)\).  When compatible, the all-zero joint-intervention risk has the sharp closed interval \([\max\{a,b,a+b-pr\},\min\{a+1-p,b+1-r,a+b+(1-p)(1-r)\}]\).  One common deterministic outcome law with independent binary-valued source roots and at most eight private-root atoms attains every real interval point; rational inputs have exact rational endpoint certificates, yielding a constant-time fixed-graph procedure and an optional conservative outer sampling interval.

project_justification.gap: General discrete-SCM methods can optimize this query sharply by a polynomial program, and causal-marginal methods explain why overlapping reports must be compatible, but the checked literature does not supply this graph-specific closed-simplex frontier, its analytic endpoints, or the small common-SCM witness.
project_justification.niche: For this fixed binary collider and intervention menu, four natural-treatment strata expose the exact obstruction, while the product law of the two latent sources rules out unrestricted latent coupling and must be retained in every attaining model.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the closed-simplex two-mass fiber, its source-preserving finite extension with explicit null-stratum branches, the resulting iff test and max--min sharp interval, and exact endpoint certificates.  This is an analytic specialization for the same fixed input handled by Autobounds, not a new general bounding compiler.

body.related_work: Duarte et al., JASA 2024, prove sharp finite-discrete causal bounds through generic polynomial programs with product disturbance probabilities and observational or experimental constraints, and implement that workflow in Autobounds.  Their theorem covers supplied categorical laws without a strict-positivity restriction; the present binary two-source collider is therefore a same-input closed-simplex specialization.  What is new here is not generic sharpness, but the derived compatibility inequality, closed-form endpoint map, and at-most-eight-atom common-SCM certificates that replace generic optimization for this one menu.  Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim prove finite canonical SCM sufficiency for categorical counterfactual distributions, but their general reduction does not yield this source-preserving certificate size or these formulas.  Gresele et al. study compatibility of overlapping causal marginals, while Sachs et al. and Finkelstein and Shpitser provide neighboring response-function and logical-bound machinery; none of the checked statements gives this collider result.  Zaffalon et al., IJAR 2023, fuse observational, biased, and randomized sources to obtain approximate counterfactual ranges, making their work adjacent multi-source bounding rather than an exact theorem-level comparator.  Autobounds is the concrete software consumer: for this fixed graph, tables, and all-zero intervention query, the analytic certificate can serve as a special-case dispatch and regression oracle.  No package modification or runtime benchmark is claimed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The source-preserving step is now constructive on every support face: feasibility forces a zero success numerator whenever its stratum mass is zero, and null observed rows use explicit arbitrary response values.  The proof uses one common deterministic \(fY\), one private threshold root \(W0\), and mutually independent, possibly degenerate, source roots \(U0,V0\), and it verifies all eight experimental cells.  The product-source restriction remains load-bearing: a correlated source model can escape the interval.  The at-most-eight support count is sufficient, not proved minimal, and the optional sampling interval is conservative rather than tie-optimal.
body.honest_scope: The result covers arbitrary normalized binary \(2\times2\) experimental tables, including structural zeros and \(p,r\in\{0,1\}\), for the fixed collider, the two stated intervention tables, mutually independent source roots, private outcome noise, and the single risk \(P_M(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0,Z=0))\).  Correlated or dependence-budget sources, different study populations, a simultaneous region for all four joint-intervention risks, three or more parents, an optimal-support theorem, tie-optimal inference, a general thicket compiler, and any field-tier claim remain excluded.  For compatible inputs, the interior width observation \(qU-qL\ge w11>0\) is asserted only when \(0<p,r<1\); boundary faces may have \(w11=0\) and can point-identify the risk.
